transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I really appreciate you taking the time. I hope I'm not being a bother, but my wife thought I should come in. 

I suppose I'm here because... well, my sleep has just gotten a bit off track lately. Is it alright if we start with that? It's probably nothing major, really, but it feels completely unmoored. A little while ago, I was waking up after just two or three hours, but I actually felt wonderful—I was up drafting all these plans, feeling completely ready to go. I thought I was just being incredibly productive, you know? 

But lately... well, now I just lie awake way before dawn. My stomach gets all tight, and I don't feel rested at all anymore. I'm sorry if that sounds a bit trivial to bring to a specialist, but it's been quite exhausting. Am I making sense?
During that time when you were sleeping only two or three hours and still felt wonderful, did you also feel unusually high or euphoric?

Euphoric... well, I suppose that might be a bit of a strong word, but... yes, I did feel wonderfully good. For a few weeks there, I felt almost brilliantly optimistic. It was as if every little obstacle in my path was just entirely trivial. I felt very capable, you know? I hope that doesn't sound arrogant. 

But, um... I do feel a bit embarrassed to admit the other side of it. I hope you won't think terribly of me, but... if anyone questioned my plans, my wife especially, I... well, I snapped at them. Quite sharply. Which isn't like me at all, really. I just felt like they were trying to sabotage things, as if I were the only sensible man in the room and everyone else was just dragging their feet. 

It's quite dreadful to look back on how irritable I was with her. Am I explaining that alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
During that time when you felt wonderfully good, did you ever believe something that other people said was clearly not true?

Oh, no, nothing like that. I mean, I hope I haven't given the impression that I was... out of touch with reality, or anything of that sort. I was just very enthusiastic about my projects, you see. 

I certainly didn't have any strange beliefs or... or think things that weren't true. I was just full of ideas, perhaps a bit too many of them, and I was quite eager to get them all done. I might have been a bit overly optimistic about how quickly I could accomplish things, but I didn't believe anything bizarre. Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm answering your question properly. I don't want you to think I'm holding anything back, but I really didn't experience anything like that.
During that time when you felt unusually good and slept very little, were you hospitalized because of it?

Oh, goodness, no. Hospitalized? No, no, nothing like that, thank heavens. I hope my description didn't make it sound as though things were completely out of hand. I was just... very energetic, that's all. 

I certainly didn't need to be in a hospital. I was at home the entire time, just working away in my study. I'm sorry if I gave the wrong impression earlier. I really was managing quite well on my own, aside from being a bit short-tempered with my wife. I hope that's the sort of answer you were looking for? I just want to be sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of how things were.
During that period when you felt unusually good and needed very little sleep, did it cause serious problems in your life or work?

Well... I suppose "serious problems" is... it's a very strong phrase, isn't it? I wouldn't say things were entirely ruined, but... yes, it did cause some difficulties. I hope you won't think I'm completely irresponsible, but I did let a few things slip. 

I usually volunteer at the museum, and I'm on the local arts council, but during those weeks... I just stopped going. I was so caught up in my own projects at home that I didn't show up reliably for them, or for my friends, really. I feel terrible about it now, of course. 

And, um... my wife, she... well, she felt she had to step in. I might have been spending a bit too freely on my new ideas, so she took over the finances. Just temporarily, you understand. And she insisted on staying close by me, just to make sure I was... safe, as she put it. I suppose I was a bit much to handle. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not painting too dreadful a picture of myself. I really do try to be reliable, normally.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Well, no... no, I haven't. I mean, everyone has an off day here and there, don't they? But certainly not for two whole weeks. 

I've always prided myself on keeping a rather positive outlook on life, really. I wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who just sits around feeling sorry for himself or... or wallows in sadness. If I ever feel a bit blue, I just try to push through it and stay busy. I think it's so important to keep your chin up. So, no, nothing at all like feeling depressed all day for weeks on end. 

Is that... does that answer what you're asking? I just want to be as helpful as I can and make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
During that unusually energetic period, did it impair your functioning so much that you couldn't manage your usual responsibilities?

Well, as I was mentioning a moment ago, I suppose it did affect things to a degree. I wouldn't use the word "impair," though—that makes it sound so terribly severe, doesn't it? But, yes, I suppose I couldn't manage everything quite the way I normally do.

Like I said, I did stop showing up for my volunteer work at the museum and the arts council. And I wasn't very reliable with my friends, either. I feel awful about that, truly I do. I just got so wrapped up in my own thoughts. 

And, of course, my wife stepping in... well, she did take over the finances because of my spending, and she felt she needed to stay with me for safety. So, I suppose I wasn't managing my usual responsibilities perfectly. But I hope you understand it wasn't out of malice or laziness—I just got a bit carried away. Am I explaining that clearly enough for you? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

latest_inference.note: Clear manic syndrome with markedly elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, increased activity/spending, and significant functional impairment requiring wife to take over finances and monitor safety; no psychotic symptoms and no hospitalization. Bipolar manic episode remains possible in lifetime terms, but no history of depressive episodes was elicited, so current best diagnosis narrows to a single manic episode without psychotic symptoms.
